subsystems.name: Photon sources
subsystems.role: generate the individual photons or squeezed light pulses that act as qubits.
parts: single-photon sources (quantum dots, spontaneous parametric down-conversion)

subsystems.name: Entanglement generation
subsystems.role: create the large entangled cluster state that defines the computation.

subsystems.name: Cluster state storage and routing
subsystems.role: hold and route the entangled state until each qubit is measured.

subsystems.name: Measurement and detection
subsystems.role: perform single-qubit measurements in bases chosen by the algorithm.

subsystems.name: Classical feed-forward and control
subsystems.role: interpret measurement outcomes and adapt later measurements in real time.

subsystems.name: Error correction and fault tolerance
subsystems.role: detect and correct errors so that logical qubits survive long enough to compute.

buildSteps.title: Generate photonic qubits
buildSteps.detail: Create single photons or squeezed vacuum states with high purity and indistinguishability, typically at telecom wavelengths around 1550 nm to minimise fiber loss.

buildSteps.title: Entangle qubits into a cluster state
buildSteps.detail: Use probabilistic fusion gates or beam splitters to entangle photons, with success heralded by detection events.

buildSteps.title: Build a large cluster state
buildSteps.detail: Multiplex many probabilistic entangling operations, using optical delay lines to synchronise photons, and stitch together a 2D or 3D lattice of entanglement.

buildSteps.title: Store and route the cluster state
buildSteps.detail: Keep the entangled photons in low-loss delay lines or waveguides until each qubit is due to be measured.

buildSteps.title: Measure qubits adaptively
buildSteps.detail: Perform single-qubit measurements in bases determined by earlier outcomes, using fast feed-forward to implement any desired circuit.

buildSteps.title: Detect and process outcomes
buildSteps.detail: Record measurement results and feed them forward within the coherence time to control subsequent measurements.

buildSteps.title: Implement error correction
buildSteps.detail: Encode logical qubits into topological cluster states and repeatedly measure stabilisers to detect and correct errors.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Integrate sources, waveguides, and detectors on photonic chips and connect modules via optical links to reach millions of qubits.

prerequisites.why: detection inefficiency and loss look like errors, so fault tolerance requires efficiencies above 99%.

prerequisites.tech: Deterministic or near-deterministic photonic entangling gates
prerequisites.why: probabilistic gates require many attempts and heavy multiplexing, which multiplies hardware and loss.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss optical components and delay lines
prerequisites.why: the cluster state must survive long enough for all measurements to be completed.
adaptive measurements must be applied within the coherence time of the photonic qubits.
physical error rates must fall below a threshold for logical qubits to be reliable at scale.
millions of components must be integrated with low loss, high uniformity and manufacturable yield.

pathway.milestone: small cluster states of a few photons demonstrated; basic measurement-based operations performed
pathway.unlocks: proof that the model works in the lab and guides component improvements.

pathway.milestone: source and detector efficiencies improved to reach fault-tolerance thresholds; error correction demonstrated on a few logical qubits
modular scaling using chip-based photonics and optical interconnects between modules
pathway.unlocks: growth to hundreds or thousands of physical qubits without a single monolithic chip.
practical quantum simulation, cryptography and optimisation beyond classical capability.
